### Capability signals

polyhierarchy taxonomy of reverse-engineering categories and tools
toolchain stage maps (acquire, identify, extract, analyze-static, observe-dynamic, validate, document)
axis tagging (target, format, architecture, method, objective, tool-role, environment, evidence)
validator-enforced placement (ops/reverse_engineering/taxonomy.py)

### Scoped question

Our v1 (PR #2145, merged 6e8e955ad1) adapts a collaborator's taxonomy example into a validated machine registry (37 nodes, 8 toolchains). What should v2 change? Specifically: (1) missing target families or tools — iOS bytecode, WASM-first chains, symbolic/concolic analysis, managed-code beyond JVM/DEX/CLR; (2) axis-vocabulary gaps measured against the field's own standards — the Kali tool catalog, MITRE ATT&CK as an added classification layer, OWASP WSTG/ASVS for the web-client chain; (3) whether the qualitative overlap matrix (central/supporting/peripheral) should become measured fleet usage, and what evidence would ground it; (4) any category errors of the kind v1 was built to prevent (platform vs discipline vs credential vs format) still present in v1's placements.

### Evidence and sources

docs/ops/REVERSE-ENGINEERING-TAXONOMY.md (v1 rationale + diff vs the collaborator example)
